Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Two-year change in depressive symptoms (GDS-15) did not differ between the vitamin B12 plus folic acid group and placebo; both tablets contained vitamin D3, so vitamin D was not the contrast.
Sentence: "Hcy concentrations decreased more in the intervention group, but two-year change scores of the GDS-15 and three of four HR-QoL measures did not differ between groups."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (GDS-15)
Population: Older adults aged 65 years or more with homocysteine concentrations of 12 µmol/L or higher
Intervention: 500 µg vitamin B12 and 400 µg folic acid daily for two years, plus 15 µg vitamin D3
Comparator: Placebo tablet containing 15 µg vitamin D3
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 2,919
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher 25OHD was associated with lower HDRS depression scores after treatment in all patients treated for depression.
Sentence: "We observed a negative correlation between the 25OHD and HDRS score after treatment in all patients treated for depression and in subgroups of women and subjects with recurrent depression."
Measured as: HDRS score after treatment
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: None (correlation across participants)
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
